material_gaps: Partial-scope conflict not resolvable from held text: EO 11708 sec. 3 revokes EO 11248 'as amended' 'except with respect to the positions enumerated in section 2', and sec. 2(3) continues 'Assistant Secretary, Comptroller, Department of Health, Education, and Welfare' in level V; EO 11251 added 'Comptroller, Department of Health, Education, and Welfare' (very probably the same position under a later title, but not shown by any held source). Whether EO 11251's single addition survived the 1973 revocation is therefore unknown.
If it survived, no held instrument shows when the continued level-V placement ended (Executive Schedule later governed by statute and later orders); no held CURRENT: predicate.

rationale: BLOCKED. I read the complete held EO 11251 (30 FR 13427, Oct. 19, 1965): one sentence amending sec. 2 of EO 11248 (Federal Executive Salary Schedule) by adding item (3), 'Comptroller, Department of Health, Education, and Welfare'; no own term and no savings clause. The 1989 Codification row says 'Superseded by EO 11708'. I read the held EO 11708 (38 FR 7979, March 23, 1973; Executive Schedule levels IV and V): secs. 1-2 place and 'continue in level V' a list of positions, and sec. 3 provides 'Except with respect to the positions enumerated in section 2 of this order, Executive Order No. 11248 of October 10, 1965, as amended, is hereby revoked.' That is a partial revocation with an express exception. The Comptroller of HEW appears in the exception list (sec. 2(3), under the title 'Assistant Secretary, Comptroller'), so 11251's lone addition may have been preserved rather than revoked, at least until some later change. The 1989 'superseded' label and the catalog note do not resolve this; they are leads. About thirty-four other amending orders in the chain (EO 11262 to 11699) are other position additions to EO 11248, not endings of 11251. I decline both statuses. To settle: the history of the HEW Comptroller position at level V after March 1973 (later executive-schedule orders or the statute that took over the schedule) and confirmation that the 1965 and 1973 titles denote the same position.
